components.note: 辶 (movement, road) — 辶 marks going and moving, as in 过, 进, 送; 迷 is losing one's way.
米 (mǐ) — near sound — 迷 is mí, the same syllable with a different tone.

example.hanzi: 我在大城市里迷路了。
example.pinyin: Wǒ zài dà chéngshì lǐ mílù le.
example.english: I got lost in the big city.
example.fact: 迷 covers being lost (迷路) and being obsessed: 球迷 (football fan), 影迷 (film fan), 歌迷 (music fan). 迷信 means superstition and 着迷 means to be captivated.

examples.hanzi: 我今天迷了路，找不到回家的路。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ jīntiān mí le lù, zhǎo bu dào huí jiā de lù.
examples.english: I got lost today and couldn't find my way home.

examples.hanzi: 他是一个足球迷。
examples.pinyin: Tā shì yí gè zúqiú mí.
examples.english: He is a football fan.

components.note: ⺮ (bamboo, 竹字头) — bamboo and written things: 笔, 第, 筷; 笨 first named a bamboo layer, then clumsy.
本 (běn) is a near sound match for bèn.

example.hanzi: 我真笨，又忘了带钥匙。
example.pinyin: Wǒ zhēn bèn, yòu wàng le dài yàoshi.
example.english: I'm so dumb, I forgot my keys again.
example.fact: 笨 means slow-witted or clumsy, milder than 傻 and often used in self-deprecation. It also describes bulk: 笨重 means heavy and awkward. The proverb 笨鸟先飞 (the slow bird flies first) praises extra effort.

examples.hanzi: 他笨手笨脚，把杯子打碎了。
examples.pinyin: Tā bèn shǒu bèn jiǎo, bǎ bēizi dǎsuì le.
examples.english: He is clumsy and smashed the cup.

examples.hanzi: 我这么笨，学不会这个。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zhème bèn, xué bu huì zhège.
examples.english: I'm so slow that I can't learn this.

components.note: 土 (earth) — marks soil and ground, as in 地 ground, 城 city wall, 坏 broken; 塔 is a tower, built from earth or brick.
荅 (dá) — loose sound hint (tǎ vs dá); same part in 答 dá.

example.hanzi: 我们爬上了那座塔。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen pá shàng le nà zuò tǎ.
example.english: We climbed that tower.
example.fact: 塔 was coined to write the Sanskrit stupa that came with Buddhism, so Chinese pagodas are 塔. The measure word is 座. It now covers any tower: 铁塔, 电视塔, and 埃菲尔铁塔 (the Eiffel Tower).

examples.hanzi: 那座塔有一百米高。
examples.pinyin: Nà zuò tǎ yǒu yìbǎi mǐ gāo.
examples.english: That tower is one hundred metres high.

examples.hanzi: 我们去爬塔，看看城市的风景。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen qù pá tǎ, kànkan chéngshì de fēngjǐng.
examples.english: Let's climb the tower and look at the city view.

components.note: 月 (flesh/meat, not moon here) — oldest form is a hand holding a piece of meat, "to possess"; 月 as meat also appears in 肉 words like 肚 belly and 脑 brain.
白 (white, bright) — 的 first meant bright and clear, as in 的确 dí què.
勺 (sháo) is a loose sound clue for dì; 勺 also sounds out 约 yuē and 钓 diào.

example.hanzi: 有的人喜欢咖啡,有的人喜欢茶。
example.pinyin: Yǒude rén xǐhuan kāfēi, yǒude rén xǐhuan chá.
example.english: Some people like coffee, some like tea.
example.fact: 有的 is a bound word that needs a noun to attach to (有的人 "some people") or a doubled frame (有的...,有的...) to split a group into subsets — unlike English "some," it rarely opens a clause on its own without a following noun.

examples.hanzi: 有的同学已经交作业了,有的还没写完。
examples.pinyin: Yǒu de tóngxué yǐjīng jiāo zuòyè le, yǒu de hái méi xiěwán.
examples.english: Some students have turned in their homework, and some haven't finished.

examples.hanzi: 桌子上有的是水果,你随便吃。
examples.pinyin: Zhuōzi shang yǒu de shì shuǐguǒ, nǐ suíbiàn chī.
examples.english: There's plenty of fruit on the table, help yourself.

components.note: 辶 (walk) — movement and roads, as in 这 this, 过 pass, 近 near; a 道 is a road, then a way or principle.
首 (shǒu, head) is only a loose sound hint for dào; 首 also means "head/first", fitting a lead-the-way road.
王 (jade) — jade and gems, as in 球 ball, 玩 play, 现 appear: 理 first meant polishing jade along its grain, then reason.
里 (lǐ) gives the exact sound; also in 鲤 lǐ.

example.hanzi: 你说的话很有道理。
example.pinyin: Nǐ shuō de huà hěn yǒu dàoli.
example.english: What you said makes a lot of sense.
example.fact: 道 ("the Way, a path") plus 理 ("the grain or pattern in jade, principle") combine into "the underlying pattern of the Way" — a compound with deep Daoist and philosophical roots that has flattened, in everyday speech, into the much more mundane "reason, common sense" of 有道理.

examples.hanzi: 这个道理很简单,大家都明白。
examples.pinyin: Zhège dàolǐ hěn jiǎndān, dàjiā dōu míngbai.
examples.english: This reason is simple and everyone understands it.

examples.hanzi: 他说得有道理,我们就听他的吧。
examples.pinyin: Tā shuō de yǒu dàolǐ, wǒmen jiù tīng tā de ba.
examples.english: He has a point, so let's follow his advice.

components.note: 舟 (boat) — 舟 is the boat radical, as in 般, 航, 舰; 船 is a ship.
长 (long, grow) — simplified from 長, an old person with long hair. Read cháng "long" or zhǎng "to grow, elder".

example.hanzi: 船长下令所有船员到甲板上集合。
example.pinyin: Chuánzhǎng xiàlìng suǒyǒu chuányuán dào jiǎbǎn shàng jíhé.
example.english: The captain ordered all crew members to assemble on deck.
example.fact: 长 is read zhǎng ("head, chief") here, not cháng ("long") — one of Mandarin's clearest multiple-reading traps, since the same character splits into two unrelated pronunciations depending on meaning, and shows up again in 校长 (xiàozhǎng, "principal") and 队长 (duìzhǎng, "team leader").

examples.hanzi: 船长站在船头,看着前方的大海。
examples.pinyin: Chuánzhǎng zhàn zài chuántóu, kàn zhe qiánfāng de dàhǎi.
examples.english: The captain stood at the bow, looking at the sea ahead.

examples.hanzi: 这位船长有三十年的航海经验。
examples.pinyin: Zhè wèi chuánzhǎng yǒu sānshí nián de hánghǎi jīngyàn.
examples.english: This captain has thirty years of sailing experience.

components.note: 欠 (yawn, open mouth) — 欠 shows a person with an open mouth, as in 吹 blow, 欢 joyful; 歌 is the mouth opened in song.
哥 (gē) — same sound — 歌 is gē, just like 哥; 哥 means elder brother.
手 (hand) — a picture of a hand with fingers spread. As a left-hand radical it becomes 扌 in 打 hit, 拿 take, 推 push.

example.hanzi: 她从小就想当一名歌手。
example.pinyin: Tā cóngxiǎo jiù xiǎng dāng yì míng gēshǒu.
example.english: She has wanted to be a singer since she was little.
example.fact: 手 as a suffix meaning "a skilled person who does X" recurs across profession words — 选手 ("athlete"), 水手 ("sailor"), 助手 ("assistant") — extending the literal "hand" into "a hand at doing something," similar to the English idiom "a good hand at X."

examples.hanzi: 我最喜欢的歌手明年要开演唱会。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zuì xǐhuan de gēshǒu míngnián yào kāi yǎnchànghuì.
examples.english: My favorite singer is giving a concert next year.

examples.hanzi: 这个歌手唱得又好听又有感情。
examples.pinyin: Zhège gēshǒu chàng de yòu hǎotīng yòu yǒu gǎnqíng.
examples.english: This singer sings beautifully and with feeling.

meanings: high ranking officer in Chinese army

components.note: 上 (above) — a mark above a line, the mirror of 下 below.
木 (tree) — wood and trees, as in 树, 林, 桌: 校 first meant a wooden frame or restraint.
交 (jiāo) is a close sound clue for xiào; 交 also in 较 jiào and 校 xiào.

example.hanzi: 他被授予上校军衔。
example.pinyin: Tā bèi shòuyǔ shàngxiào jūnxián.
example.english: He was awarded the rank of colonel.
example.fact: Chinese military officer ranks are built from three base grades — 尉 (company-grade), 校 (field-grade) and 将 (general) — each split into 上/中/少 ("upper/middle/junior"), so 上校 "colonel" is structurally the upper tier of the 校 grade, parallel to 上尉 and 上将, rather than an unrelated standalone word.

examples.hanzi: 上校命令部队向前出发。
examples.pinyin: Shàngxiào mìnglìng bùduì xiàng qián chūfā.
examples.english: The colonel ordered the troops to move forward.

examples.hanzi: 我爷爷年轻的时候是一名上校。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ yéye niánqīng de shíhou shì yì míng shàngxiào.
examples.english: My grandfather was a colonel when he was young.

components.note: 扌 (hand radical, 提手旁) — actions by hand: 打, 拉, 推; 撒 is scattering or letting go.
散 (sàn) scatter is the meaning-sound part: a hand 扌 scattering, with sā/sàn close in sound.

example.hanzi: 他从不撒谎。
example.pinyin: Tā cóng bù sāhuǎng.
example.english: He never tells lies.
example.fact: 撒 has two readings: sā (撒谎 to lie, 撒娇 to act coy, 撒手 to let go) and sǎ (to sprinkle, as in 撒盐). In 撒谎 the verb literally means "to cast a lie".

examples.hanzi: 请别在这里撒糖，会引来蚂蚁。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng bié zài zhèlǐ sā táng, huì yǐnlái mǎyǐ.
examples.english: Please don't scatter sugar here; it will attract ants.

examples.hanzi: 他一撒手，气球就飞走了。
examples.pinyin: Tā yì sā shǒu, qìqiú jiù fēi zǒu le.
examples.english: As soon as he let go, the balloon flew away.

components.note: 辶 (walk, 走之旁) — movement and roads: 过, 进, 送; 运 is to move, then to be moved by luck.
云 (yún) is a near sound match for yùn.
气 (air, vapor) — lines of rising vapor or breath. Add water for 汽 steam; seen in 生气 get angry, 空气 air.

example.hanzi: 祝你今天运气好。
example.pinyin: Zhù nǐ jīntiān yùnqi hǎo.
example.english: Wishing you good luck today.
example.fact: When both syllables keep a full tone, yùnqì, the same two characters can instead mean "to circulate one's qi/breath" in qigong or martial-arts contexts — the everyday "luck" sense is distinguished by a neutral tone on the second syllable, yùnqi.

examples.hanzi: 他今天的运气真不错,抽到了奖。
examples.pinyin: Tā jīntiān de yùnqi zhēn búcuò, chōudào le jiǎng.
examples.english: He was really lucky today and won a prize.

examples.hanzi: 我运气不好,每次都排错队。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ yùnqi bù hǎo, měi cì dōu pái cuò duì.
examples.english: I'm unlucky and always pick the wrong line.

components.note: 主 (master, host) — a lamp with a flame on top; a lamp stand was the centre of the room. 主 also sounds out 注 zhù, 住 zhù and 柱 zhù.
要 (want, need) — oldest form shows hands at a waist: it meant "waist" (腰 yāo adds 月 flesh); "essential" followed.

example.hanzi: 这次会议的主要目的是讨论预算。
example.pinyin: Zhè cì huìyì de zhǔyào mùdì shì tǎolùn yùsuàn.
example.english: The main purpose of this meeting is to discuss the budget.
example.fact: 主 is traditionally read as a lamp's flame (丶) sitting atop its stand (王) — the person who tends that flame became "master, lord," and 主要 pairs it with 要 ("essential") to mean, roughly, "the master point" — today's ordinary word for "main, primary."

examples.hanzi: 我主要负责客户服务。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zhǔyào fùzé kèhù fúwù.
examples.english: I'm mainly responsible for customer service.

examples.hanzi: 他迟到的主要原因是堵车。
examples.pinyin: Tā chídào de zhǔyào yuányīn shì dǔchē.
examples.english: The main reason he was late was traffic.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — speech, as in 吃, 唱, 问: voices in unison. 同 also gives sound to 铜 tóng, 桶 tǒng, 洞 dòng.
彐 (hand-like part) — 事 is usually explained as a hand holding a tool or tally, 'handling business' — a hedged reading, not certain.
史 (history, scribe) — shares an ancient root with 事: a hand holding a recording tool. Both are about handling official 'matters'.

example.hanzi: 我和同事一起吃午饭。
example.pinyin: Wǒ hé tóngshì yìqǐ chī wǔfàn.
example.english: I have lunch with my colleagues.
example.fact: 同事 literally means "share the same affairs" (同 "same" + 事 "matter") — one of a family of "same-X" relationship words built the same way, alongside 同学 ("classmate," same study) and 同乡 ("someone from the same hometown").

examples.hanzi: 我的同事今天请假了。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ de tóngshì jīntiān qǐngjià le.
examples.english: My coworker took the day off today.

examples.hanzi: 他和同事相处得很好。
examples.pinyin: Tā hé tóngshì xiāngchǔ de hěn hǎo.
examples.english: He gets along well with his colleagues.

components.note: 食 (food) — eating and meals: 饭, 饿, 饱 (as 饣); 餐 is a meal.
厂 (shelter) — 厂 here stands for a building; the traditional 廳 had 广, a wide hall.
丁 (dīng) — near sound — 厅 is tīng; 丁 also sounds out 订 dìng and 顶 dǐng.

example.hanzi: 我们订了一家餐厅庆祝生日。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen dìng le yì jiā cāntīng qìngzhù shēngrì.
example.english: We booked a restaurant to celebrate the birthday.
example.fact: 餐厅 covers both a stand-alone commercial "restaurant" and an institutional "dining hall" inside a school, office, or hotel — for a small, casual eatery Chinese instead reaches for 饭馆 or 小吃店, so 餐厅 leans toward a larger or more formal dining space.

examples.hanzi: 这家餐厅的牛肉面很好吃。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā cāntīng de niúròu miàn hěn hǎochī.
examples.english: The beef noodles at this restaurant are very good.

examples.hanzi: 我们公司楼下有一个大餐厅。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen gōngsī lóu xià yǒu yí ge dà cāntīng.
examples.english: There's a big dining hall downstairs in our company.

components.note: 火 (fire) — 火 is fire, as in 烧, 灯, 炒; 烟 is smoke.
因 (yīn) — near sound — 烟 is yān; 因 also sounds out 姻 yīn.

example.hanzi: 他每天抽一包烟。
example.pinyin: Tā měitiān chōu yì bāo yān.
example.english: He smokes a pack of cigarettes a day.
example.fact: 烟 means smoke and cigarettes: 抽烟 or 吸烟 (to smoke). Offering a cigarette (递烟) is a classic social gesture. 烟花 (fireworks) literally means smoke-flowers.

examples.hanzi: 这里不许抽烟。
examples.pinyin: Zhèlǐ bù xǔ chōuyān.
examples.english: Smoking is not allowed here.

examples.hanzi: 屋里全是烟，我们快开窗。
examples.pinyin: Wū lǐ quán shì yān, wǒmen kuài kāi chuāng.
examples.english: The room is full of smoke; let's open the window quickly.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — marks speaking, shouting, eating and sounds, as in 叫 call, 吃 eat, 唱 sing; 喊 is to shout.
咸 (xián) — sound hint is loose now (hǎn vs xián); same part sits in 减 jiǎn and 感 gǎn.

example.hanzi: 他在门口喊我的名字。
example.pinyin: Tā zài ménkǒu hǎn wǒ de míngzi.
example.english: He called my name at the door.
example.fact: 喊 is to shout or call out for someone: 喊他过来 (call him over). It also means to address someone as: 喊他叔叔 (call him uncle). 喊口号 means to chant slogans.

examples.hanzi: 他在山上大声喊。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài shānshang dàshēng hǎn.
examples.english: He shouted loudly on the mountain.

examples.hanzi: 请喊他来接电话。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng hǎn tā lái jiē diànhuà.
examples.english: Please call him to the phone.

components.note: 各 (each) — a foot 夂 arriving at a place 口: each one coming. 各 also sounds out 路 lù, 格 gé, 客 kè and 洛 luò.

example.hanzi: 各位同学，请坐。
example.pinyin: Gèwèi tóngxué, qǐng zuò.
example.english: Everyone, please take a seat.
example.fact: 各 is a determiner placed before a noun: 各国 (every country), 各位 (everyone, polite), 各种 (all kinds). Compared with 每, 各 stresses that each member does its own thing: 各有各的想法.

examples.hanzi: 各位请注意，电梯马上就要关了。
examples.pinyin: Gèwèi qǐng zhùyì, diàntī mǎshàng jiù yào guān le.
examples.english: Everyone, please note that the elevator is about to close.

examples.hanzi: 各个国家的文化都不一样。
examples.pinyin: Gègè guójiā de wénhuà dōu bù yíyàng.
examples.english: Every country's culture is different.

components.note: 鬼 (ghost) — spirits and the unseen: 魂, 魅, 愧; 魔 is a demon.
麻 (má) is a near sound match for mó; also in 磨 mó and 摩 mó.

example.hanzi: 故事里有一个魔鬼。
example.pinyin: Gùshi lǐ yǒu yí ge móguǐ.
example.english: There is a devil in the story.
example.fact: 魔 was created to write Sanskrit māra (the tempter) in Buddhist texts. It gives 魔法 (magic), 魔术 (conjuring), 魔鬼 (devil) and the slang 魔怔 (obsessed).

examples.hanzi: 孩子们喜欢听魔法的故事。
examples.pinyin: Háizimen xǐhuan tīng mófǎ de gùshi.
examples.english: Children like listening to stories about magic.

examples.hanzi: 他很会变魔术，大家都爱看。
examples.pinyin: Tā hěn huì biàn móshù, dàjiā dōu ài kàn.
examples.english: He is good at magic tricks, and everyone loves watching.

components.note: 羊 (sheep) — traditionally 羊 over 大: a big, fat sheep was good, tasty and pleasing, hence beautiful. 羊 also appears in 样 and 洋.
女 (woman) — a person kneeling with arms crossed; as a radical it heads many female and family words: 妈, 好, 姐.

example.hanzi: 大家都夸她是个美女。
example.pinyin: Dàjiā dōu kuā tā shì gè měinǚ.
example.english: Everyone said she's a beautiful woman.
example.fact: 美女 has drifted from its literal "beautiful woman" into a casual, almost gender-neutral form of address across much of Mainland China — shop clerks and strangers now often call any young woman "美女" simply to get her attention, similar to how English "miss" is used regardless of looks.

examples.hanzi: 那位美女是我们公司的新同事。
examples.pinyin: Nà wèi měinǚ shì wǒmen gōngsī de xīn tóngshì.
examples.english: That beautiful woman is our company's new colleague.

examples.hanzi: 美女,请问洗手间在哪儿?
examples.pinyin: Měinǚ, qǐngwèn xǐshǒujiān zài nǎr?
examples.english: Excuse me, miss, where's the restroom?

components.note: 足 (foot) — 足 (⻊) marks feet and walking, as in 跑, 跳, 路; 距 is the gap between two steps.
巨 (jù) — same sound — 距 is jù; 巨 also sounds out 拒 jù and 矩 jǔ.
離 (traditional) — 隹 (bird) plus 离 as sound (lí). 离 was an old name for a mythical beast, so the 'leave' sense comes from 離; 离 kept only the sound part.

example.hanzi: 这两个城市之间的距离大约是三百公里。
example.pinyin: Zhè liǎng gè chéngshì zhījiān de jùlí dàyuē shì sānbǎi gōnglǐ.
example.english: The distance between these two cities is about three hundred kilometers.
example.fact: 距离 doubles as both a noun ("distance") and a verb ("to be apart from," as in 距离现在 "counting from now") — a common Mandarin pattern where a compound describing a spatial or temporal relationship can function like a preposition without needing a separate word.

examples.hanzi: 学校离我家的距离很近。
examples.pinyin: Xuéxiào lí wǒ jiā de jùlí hěn jìn.
examples.english: The school is a short distance from my home.

examples.hanzi: 保持一米的距离,别靠得太近。
examples.pinyin: Bǎochí yì mǐ de jùlí, bié kào de tài jìn.
examples.english: Keep a distance of one meter, don't get too close.

components.note: 龶 (plant-like top) — dictionary reads the top as 'a poisonous plant'. Memory aid: a plant growing on top of a mother (母) is something you must not eat.
母 (mǔ, mother) — the bottom part and radical. Sound clue is lost today (毒 is dú); use it as a visual memory aid, as in 母亲.

example.hanzi: 这种蘑菇有毒。
example.pinyin: Zhè zhǒng mógu yǒu dú.
example.english: This kind of mushroom is poisonous.
example.fact: 毒 covers poison and drugs: 有毒 (toxic), 吸毒 (to take drugs), 毒品 (narcotics). 病毒 (virus) is literally "illness poison". As an adjective it can mean cruel: 毒蛇 and 狠毒.

examples.hanzi: 别吃这个，里面有毒。
examples.pinyin: Bié chī zhège, lǐmiàn yǒu dú.
examples.english: Don't eat this; it's poisonous.

examples.hanzi: 吸烟对身体有毒害。
examples.pinyin: Xīyān duì shēntǐ yǒu dúhài.
examples.english: Smoking is toxic to your body.

components.note: 讠 (speech) — 讠 is the simplified 言 (speech), as in 说, 话, 读; 讲 is to talk and explain.
井 (jǐng) — near sound — 讲 is jiǎng; the old form had a different right side, so this is only a loose hint.
讠 (speech) — words and language, as in 说, 请, 谢; 话 is speech.
舌 (shé, tongue) fits the meaning (speaking) and is a loose sound clue for huà; also in 活 huó.

example.hanzi: 校长在开学典礼上讲话。
example.pinyin: Xiàozhǎng zài kāixué diǎnlǐ shàng jiǎnghuà.
example.english: The principal gave a speech at the opening ceremony.
example.fact: 讲话 leans formal and public — a speech given at a ceremony or meeting — while its near-synonym 说话 is the neutral, everyday verb for ordinary talking; mixing the two up is a common register slip when narrating a meeting versus a casual chat.

examples.hanzi: 他在台上讲话的时候一点儿也不紧张。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài tái shang jiǎnghuà de shíhou yìdiǎnr yě bù jǐnzhāng.
examples.english: He wasn't nervous at all while speaking on the stage.

examples.hanzi: 请大家安静,经理要讲话了。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng dàjiā ānjìng, jīnglǐ yào jiǎnghuà le.
examples.english: Everyone quiet please, the manager is about to speak.

components.note: 月 (flesh/meat, not moon here) — oldest form is a hand holding a piece of meat, "to possess"; 月 as meat also appears in 肉 words like 肚 belly and 脑 brain.
斤 (axe) — cutting tools, as in 新 new and 斩 chop. 所 once echoed the sound of chopping; "place" and "that which" are later borrowed uses.

example.hanzi: 经过练习,他的水平有所提高。
example.pinyin: Jīngguò liànxí, tā de shuǐpíng yǒusuǒ tígāo.
example.english: After practice, his level improved somewhat.
example.fact: 有所 is a bound, formal adverb that must be followed by a two-syllable verb (有所提高 "improved somewhat," 有所了解 "have some understanding") — it never attaches to a one-syllable verb or stands alone, marking it as bookish, written-register vocabulary rather than casual speech.

examples.hanzi: 这几个月他的成绩有所进步。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jǐ ge yuè tā de chéngjì yǒusuǒ jìnbù.
examples.english: His grades have improved somewhat in recent months.

examples.hanzi: 天气预报说明天气温会有所下降。
examples.pinyin: Tiānqì yùbào shuō míngtiān qìwēn huì yǒusuǒ xiàjiàng.
examples.english: The weather forecast says the temperature will drop somewhat tomorrow.

components.note: 刂 (knife) — cutting, as in 到, 分, 别: 制 is cutting to shape, then to make and to control.
亻 (person) — people, as in 你, 他, 做: 作 is something a person does or makes.
乍 (zuò) gives the exact sound; 乍 also in 昨 zuó, 炸 zhà and 怎 zěn.

example.hanzi: 这部动画是由一家日本公司制作的。
example.pinyin: Zhè bù dònghuà shì yóu yì jiā Rìběn gōngsī zhìzuò de.
example.english: This animated film was produced by a Japanese company.
example.fact: 制作 implies a deliberate, often skilled or artistic process — used for films, handicrafts, or designed goods — distinguishing it from the more mechanical, bulk-scale 生产 ("to manufacture"), a distinction that matters when describing anything from a documentary to a factory product.

examples.hanzi: 她正在制作一个生日蛋糕。
examples.pinyin: Tā zhèngzài zhìzuò yí ge shēngrì dàngāo.
examples.english: She is making a birthday cake.

examples.hanzi: 这家工作室专门制作广告视频。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā gōngzuòshì zhuānmén zhìzuò guǎnggào shìpín.
examples.english: This studio specializes in making advertising videos.

components.note: 行 (go, road) — 行 (walk, go) splits around the middle — 街 is a road; compare 往 go and 衔.
圭 (guī) — loose hint only — 街 is jiē.
上 (above) — a mark above a line, the mirror of 下 below.

example.hanzi: 街上到处都是卖小吃的摊子。
example.pinyin: Jiēshang dàochù dōu shì mài xiǎochī de tānzi.
example.english: The street is full of snack stalls everywhere.
example.fact: 上 as a locative suffix (街上, 桌子上, 床上) turns a bare place-noun into "on/at [place]" — one of Mandarin's most productive grammar patterns for building location phrases, standing in for the prepositions English would use instead.

examples.hanzi: 我昨天在街上看到了你的老师。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zuótiān zài jiē shang kàndào le nǐ de lǎoshī.
examples.english: I saw your teacher on the street yesterday.

examples.hanzi: 街上有很多人在庆祝节日。
examples.pinyin: Jiē shang yǒu hěn duō rén zài qìngzhù jiérì.
examples.english: Many people are celebrating the holiday on the street.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — to throw down by hand; also in 打 hit, 扔 throw.
率 (shuài) gives the same syllable with a different tone.

example.hanzi: 他从自行车上摔下来了。
example.pinyin: Tā cóng zìxíngchē shang shuāi xiàlai le.
example.english: He fell off his bike.
example.fact: 摔 covers an accidental fall (摔倒) and a deliberate throw (摔东西, to smash things). It is more forceful than 掉. 摔跤 can mean either wrestling or a tumble.

examples.hanzi: 小心，别摔倒了。
examples.pinyin: Xiǎoxīn, bié shuāidǎo le.
examples.english: Careful, don't fall over.

examples.hanzi: 他把手机摔坏了。
examples.pinyin: Tā bǎ shǒujī shuāihuài le.
examples.english: He dropped his phone and broke it.

components.note: 囗 (enclosure) — boundaries: 国, 园, 围; 团 is a round group. Its traditional form had 專 as sound, like 转 zhuǎn and 传 chuán.
阝 (mound, left-side form of 阜 hill) — hills and places: 院, 阳, 陆; 队 is a group of people gathered together.

example.hanzi: 这个项目需要整个团队的努力。
example.pinyin: Zhège xiàngmù xūyào zhěnggè tuánduì de nǔlì.
example.english: This project needs the effort of the whole team.
example.fact: 团队 doubles up two words that both independently mean "a group" — 团 ("a group, a round mass," as in 团体) and 队 ("a line, a squad," as in 队伍) — reinforcing each other into one compound, the same word-building strategy behind 喜欢.

examples.hanzi: 这是我们团队第一次一起出差。
examples.pinyin: Zhè shì wǒmen tuánduì dì yī cì yìqǐ chūchāi.
examples.english: This is our team's first business trip together.

examples.hanzi: 团队合作比个人能力更重要。
examples.pinyin: Tuánduì hézuò bǐ gèrén nénglì gèng zhòngyào.
examples.english: Teamwork matters more than individual ability.

components.note: 日 (sun) — time and day, as in 时, 晚, 明: the sun at the top of a sprout, early morning. 早 also gives 草 cǎo and 澡 zǎo.
京 (jīng, high mound, capital) is a loose sound clue for jiù; going up to a high place fits 就 "to approach, to go to".

example.hanzi: 我早就跟你说过这件事了。
example.pinyin: Wǒ zǎojiù gēn nǐ shuōguò zhè jiàn shì le.
example.english: I told you about this a long time ago.
example.fact: 早就 stresses that something happened well before the relevant reference point, often with a hint of "I told you so" — its plainer cousin 已经 simply marks that an action is complete, without that extra emphasis on how far back in time it happened.

examples.hanzi: 他早就知道了,只是没告诉你。
examples.pinyin: Tā zǎojiù zhīdào le, zhǐshì méi gàosu nǐ.
examples.english: He knew long ago, he just didn't tell you.

examples.hanzi: 我早就想去那家店尝一尝了。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zǎojiù xiǎng qù nà jiā diàn cháng yi cháng le.
examples.english: I've been wanting to try that shop for ages.

components.note: 自 (self, nose) — 自 originally pictured a nose — pointing to it meant "me", as in 自己; 鼻 adds 畀 for sound.
畀 (bì) — near sound — 鼻 is bí.
子 (child) — a picture of a baby with arms outstretched and legs bundled. As a suffix (孩子, 房子) it is a light noun ending.

example.hanzi: 小孩子好奇地摸了摸自己的鼻子。
example.pinyin: Xiǎo háizi hàoqí de mō le mō zìjǐ de bízi.
example.english: The child curiously touched his own nose.
example.fact: 鼻 alone already means "nose," built from 自 (originally itself a pictograph of a nose, later reassigned to mean "self") plus the phonetic 畀 — 子 is then added purely as the familiar noun-suffix seen in 孩子, turning a formal root into the everyday spoken word.

examples.hanzi: 他感冒了,鼻子一直不通。
examples.pinyin: Tā gǎnmào le, bízi yìzhí bù tōng.
examples.english: He has a cold and his nose is stuffed up.

examples.hanzi: 这只大象的鼻子又长又灵活。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhī dàxiàng de bízi yòu cháng yòu línghuó.
examples.english: This elephant's trunk is long and flexible.

components.note: 目 (eye) — looking; an eye turned on a tree 木, hence to look at, and mutually looking: "each other". 相 also gives 想 xiǎng, 箱 xiāng and 湘 xiāng.
夂 (foot) — stopping or going: 处 first meant to stay or settle, then a place or to deal with.

example.hanzi: 他们俩相处得很融洽。
example.pinyin: Tāmen liǎ xiāngchǔ de hěn róngqià.
example.english: The two of them get along very well.
example.fact: 相 marks a mutual, reciprocal action shared between two or more parties (相处, 相爱 "to love each other," 相识 "to know each other") — it functions like a fixed reciprocal prefix similar to English "each other," and never appears with only one participant.

examples.hanzi: 我和室友相处了两年,从来没吵过架。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ hé shìyǒu xiāngchǔ le liǎng nián, cónglái méi chǎo guo jià.
examples.english: My roommate and I have lived together for two years without ever arguing.

examples.hanzi: 你们俩相处得怎么样?
examples.pinyin: Nǐmen liǎ xiāngchǔ de zěnmeyàng?
examples.english: How do you two get along?

meanings: a modal particle indicating resignation or acceptance

components.note: 罒 (net) — the top part, as in 罪 crime. Story: stuck in a net, unable to leave, hence 'stop'; in 罢了 it is just the final particle 'that's all'.
去 (go) — the bottom part, as in 法. Dictionary reading: a net blocking you from going; as memory aid.
子 (child) — 了 is usually read as a swaddled baby, like 子 without the arms. Its meanings 'finish' (了解 liǎo) and the particle le were borrowed later.

example.hanzi: 我只是开个玩笑罢了,别当真。
example.pinyin: Wǒ zhǐshì kāi gè wánxiào bàle, bié dàngzhēn.
example.english: I was just making a joke, that's all — don't take it seriously.
example.fact: 罢了 sits at the very end of a sentence to downplay what was just said, much like English "that's all" tacked on afterward — it very often pairs with an earlier 只是 or 不过 ("只是...罢了") to double down on the minimizing tone.

examples.hanzi: 我只是想帮你罢了。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zhǐshì xiǎng bāng nǐ bà le.
examples.english: I just wanted to help you, that's all.

examples.hanzi: 没什么大事,不过是一次小意外罢了。
examples.pinyin: Méi shénme dà shì, búguò shì yí cì xiǎo yìwài bà le.
examples.english: It's nothing serious, just a small accident.

components.note: 广 (building) — 广 is a building radical, as in 店, 床; 度 also sounds out 渡 dù and 镀 dù.
辶 (walk) — movement, as in 这, 近, 送: 过 is to pass or cross.
寸 here replaces 咼 (guō) of the traditional 過, so it is not a sound clue; 咼 survives in 锅 guō and 祸 huò.

example.hanzi: 他们在海边度过了愉快的暑假。
example.pinyin: Tāmen zài hǎibiān dùguò le yúkuài de shǔjià.
example.english: They spent a pleasant summer vacation at the beach.
example.fact: 度过 is reserved for living through a stretch of time (度过童年 "to spend one's childhood," 度过难关 "to get through a hard period") — it cannot be used for spending money, which instead takes 花 (花钱), a distinction that trips up learners who default to a single English verb "to spend."

examples.hanzi: 我们一起度过了难忘的一天。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen yìqǐ dùguò le nánwàng de yì tiān.
examples.english: We spent an unforgettable day together.

examples.hanzi: 医生帮他度过了危险期。
examples.pinyin: Yīshēng bāng tā dùguò le wēixiǎn qī.
examples.english: The doctor helped him get through the dangerous period.

components.note: 纟 (silk thread, simplified 糸) — threads, as in 红, 给, 经: cutting a thread, hence to break off.
色 (sè) is only a loose sound clue for jué.

example.hanzi: 他拒绝了我的邀请。
example.pinyin: Tā jùjué le wǒ de yāoqǐng.
example.english: He turned down my invitation.
example.fact: 绝 originally meant to cut a thread. It gives 拒绝 (to refuse), 绝对 (absolutely), 绝望 (despair) and 绝种 (extinct). Slang 绝了 means "amazing", used as high praise.

examples.hanzi: 我们绝对不会放弃。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen juéduì bú huì fàngqì.
examples.english: We will absolutely never give up.

examples.hanzi: 这种动物已经绝种了。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhǒng dòngwù yǐjīng juézhǒng le.
examples.english: This kind of animal has gone extinct.

components.note: 彐 (broom top, from 帚) — in the old form 歸 a woman with a broom 帚 'returns' to her husband's home; the story is a traditional account, not proven.
追 (zhuī) — the old form 歸 is said to use 追-like parts for sound; guī is only a loose match. Treat as a memory aid, not a rule.

example.hanzi: 这件事归你管。
example.pinyin: Zhè jiàn shì guī nǐ guǎn.
example.english: This matter is yours to handle.
example.fact: In modern speech 归 often means "to belong to / to be the responsibility of": 归你管, 这本书归我. In writing it means to return: 回归, 归还 (to give back), 归来 (to return home).

examples.hanzi: 他把借的书归还给图书馆。
examples.pinyin: Tā bǎ jiè de shū guīhuán gěi túshūguǎn.
examples.english: He returned the borrowed book to the library.

examples.hanzi: 这件事归我管，你不用担心。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiàn shì guī wǒ guǎn, nǐ búyòng dānxīn.
examples.english: I'm in charge of this, so you needn't worry.

components.note: 手 (hand) — marks the hand and its actions, as in 拿, 掌 palm, 摩; 拳 is the fist, a hand curled up.
龹 (a curling shape) hints at the sound: 拳 quán is close to 卷 juǎn and 圈 quān.

example.hanzi: 他握紧了拳头。
example.pinyin: Tā wò jǐn le quántou.
example.english: He clenched his fist.
example.fact: 拳 is the fist, and also boxing or martial arts: 打拳, 太极拳. It is a measure word for punches: 打了他一拳 (punched him once).

examples.hanzi: 他练了十年拳，身体很结实。
examples.pinyin: Tā liàn le shí nián quán, shēntǐ hěn jiēshi.
examples.english: He has practiced boxing for ten years and is very strong.

examples.hanzi: 他一拳打在桌子上。
examples.pinyin: Tā yì quán dǎ zài zhuōzi shang.
examples.english: He banged his fist on the table.

components.note: 关 (close) — simplified from 關, a gate 门 with a bolt across it; 关 also means "concern", as in 关系.
氵 (water) — water and pouring, as in 河, 海, 清: 注 is to pour in.
主 (zhǔ) is a close sound clue for zhù; 主 also in 住 zhù, 柱 zhù and 驻 zhù.

example.hanzi: 很多网友都在关注这条新闻。
example.pinyin: Hěn duō wǎngyǒu dōu zài guānzhù zhè tiáo xīnwén.
example.english: Many netizens are following this news story.
example.fact: With the rise of social media, 关注 picked up the specific extra sense of "to follow" an account (关注他的微博 "follow his Weibo") — much the way English "follow" was repurposed for a new online action once Twitter and Instagram adopted it.

examples.hanzi: 我们应该多关注孩子的心理健康。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen yīnggāi duō guānzhù háizi de xīnlǐ jiànkāng.
examples.english: We should pay more attention to children's mental health.

examples.hanzi: 他最近很关注环保问题。
examples.pinyin: Tā zuìjìn hěn guānzhù huánbǎo wèntí.
examples.english: He has been following environmental issues closely lately.

components.note: 彳 (step, conduct) — 彳 is a step or going, as in 行 and 往; 德 is conduct.
心 (heart) — 心 is the heart — the old 悳 was a straight 直 heart, so upright inner conduct.
囗 (enclosure) — borders and walls, as in 园 garden, 圆 round, 回 return; 囗 is the country's boundary.
玉 (jade) — treasure within the border; the traditional 國 had 或 (defended territory) inside.

example.hanzi: 他去德国留学了三年。
example.pinyin: Tā qù Déguó liúxué le sān nián.
example.english: He studied abroad in Germany for three years.
example.fact: 德 here was chosen mainly for its sound, to transliterate "Deutsch" — but since 德 independently means "virtue, morality," it's a frequently noted coincidence that pairs it with other flattering-sounding transliterated country names, like 美国 ("beautiful country") and 英国 ("hero country," see also 英尺 in this batch).

examples.hanzi: 我的朋友在德国工作,会说德语。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ de péngyou zài Déguó gōngzuò, huì shuō Déyǔ.
examples.english: My friend works in Germany and speaks German.

examples.hanzi: 德国的汽车在世界上很有名。
examples.pinyin: Déguó de qìchē zài shìjiè shang hěn yǒumíng.
examples.english: German cars are famous around the world.

components.note: 大 (big) — a front-facing person with arms and legs spread wide: big. As radical, 大 is in 天 sky, 太 too much, 夫 man.
阝 on the right is 邑 (city) — places, as in 都 capital, 邮 post, 那: a district or ministry.
咅 (pǒu) is a loose sound clue for bù; 咅 also in 剖 pōu, 培 péi and 陪 péi.
刀 (knife) — cutting, as in 切, 刻, 到: a blade splits.
八 (eight) — originally two lines pulling apart: divide. 分 also gives 份 fèn, 粉 fěn and 纷 fēn.

example.hanzi: 大部分学生都同意这个建议。
example.pinyin: Dà bùfen xuésheng dōu tóngyì zhège jiànyì.
example.english: Most students agree with this suggestion.
example.fact: 大部分 sits at the high end of a scale of Mandarin "how much" words — 一部分 ("a portion"), 一半 ("half"), 大部分 ("most, the greater part"), 全部 ("all") — letting a speaker calibrate quantity without needing an exact percentage.

examples.hanzi: 我大部分时间都在家工作。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ dà bùfen shíjiān dōu zài jiā gōngzuò.
examples.english: I work from home most of the time.

examples.hanzi: 这本书我已经看完了大部分。
examples.pinyin: Zhè běn shū wǒ yǐjīng kànwán le dà bùfen.
examples.english: I've already read most of this book.

components.note: 穴 (hole, cave) — 穴 marks holes and cavities, as in 空, 穷, 突; 窗 is an opening in a wall.
囱 (cōng) — near sound — 窗 is chuāng; 囱 also sounds out 葱 cōng and 聪 cōng.
户 (door, household) — one half of a double door 門. As a radical it marks doors and rooms: 房 room, 所 place, 扇 fan.

example.hanzi: 请把窗户打开,透透气。
example.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ chuānghu dǎkāi, tòu tou qì.
example.english: Please open the window to let some air in.
example.fact: 户 alone already means "a door, a household" (a pictograph of a single door panel), while 窗 alone already means "a window" — pairing near-synonyms this way, purely for two-syllable rhythm, is a common Mandarin compounding habit even when one half already covers the whole meaning.

examples.hanzi: 外面很吵,把窗户关上吧。
examples.pinyin: Wàimiàn hěn chǎo, bǎ chuānghu guān shang ba.
examples.english: It's noisy outside, so close the window.

examples.hanzi: 他坐在窗户旁边看书。
examples.pinyin: Tā zuò zài chuānghu pángbiān kàn shū.
examples.english: He sits by the window reading.

meanings: variant of 奇蹟|奇迹[qi2 ji4]

components.note: 奇 (qí) is a sound clue for 骑 qí, 寄 jì, 椅 yǐ and 崎 qí; as a word it means strange or remarkable.
辶 (movement, road) — 辶 marks going and moving, as in 过, 进, 送; 迹 is a footprint, as in 奇迹 miracle.
亦 (yì) — near sound — 迹 is jì; 亦 also sounds out 迹 jì.

example.hanzi: 他能活下来真是个奇迹。
example.pinyin: Tā néng huó xiàlai zhēn shì gè qíjì.
example.english: It's truly a miracle that he survived.
example.fact: 迹 means "a trace, a footprint left behind" (built from 辶, "to walk") — 奇迹 literally reads as "a strange trace," the lingering evidence of something so unusual it seems to defy explanation, which is how the word settled into meaning "miracle."

examples.hanzi: 这简直是一个奇迹!
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiǎnzhí shì yí ge qíjì!
examples.english: This is truly a miracle!

examples.hanzi: 医生说她的恢复是一个医学奇迹。
examples.pinyin: Yīshēng shuō tā de huīfù shì yí ge yīxué qíjì.
examples.english: The doctor said her recovery was a medical miracle.

components.note: 穴 (cave) — 穴 is a cave or hole, as in 窗 window, 穷 poor; 空 is empty like a hollow.
工 (gōng) — near sound — 空 is kōng; also in 红 hóng.
气 (air, vapor) — lines of rising vapor or breath. Add water for 汽 steam; seen in 生气 get angry, 空气 air.

example.hanzi: 山里的空气特别新鲜。
example.pinyin: Shān lǐ de kōngqì tèbié xīnxiān.
example.english: The air in the mountains is especially fresh.
example.fact: 空 ("empty, hollow space") plus 气 ("gas, breath, vapor") combine into "the gas that fills empty space" — a fittingly literal description of air, built from the same 气 root that appears in 天气 ("weather") and 运气 (rank 1162 in this batch, "luck").

examples.hanzi: 打开窗户,让新鲜空气进来。
examples.pinyin: Dǎkāi chuānghu, ràng xīnxiān kōngqì jìnlái.
examples.english: Open the window and let some fresh air in.

examples.hanzi: 这个房间里的空气太闷了。
examples.pinyin: Zhège fángjiān lǐ de kōngqì tài mēn le.
examples.english: The air in this room is too stuffy.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — hand actions, as in 打, 拿, 抱: guarding with the hands.
户 (hù, door) gives the exact sound; 户 means door or household.
士 (scholar, soldier) — usually read as an axe or weapon, so a warrior or gentleman (士兵, 博士). Memory aid: 士 has the longer bar on top, 土 (earth) on the bottom.

example.hanzi: 护士每天都要给病人量体温。
example.pinyin: Hùshi měitiān dōu yào gěi bìngrén liáng tǐwēn.
example.english: The nurse has to take patients' temperature every day.
example.fact: 士 as a suffix marks a trained professional or specialist (护士 "nurse," 战士 "soldier," 博士 "PhD holder") — the same root traces back to an old, respected class of literate specialists in ancient China, and also gives 士兵 "soldier" and 士气 "morale."

examples.hanzi: 这位护士对病人非常耐心。
examples.pinyin: Zhè wèi hùshi duì bìngrén fēicháng nàixīn.
examples.english: This nurse is very patient with patients.

examples.hanzi: 我姐姐想当一名护士。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ jiějie xiǎng dāng yì míng hùshi.
examples.english: My older sister wants to be a nurse.

meanings: to share (esp. sth enjoyable, useful or beneficial)

components.note: 刀 (knife) — cutting, as in 切, 刻, 到: a blade splits.
八 (eight) — originally two lines pulling apart: divide. 分 also gives 份 fèn, 粉 fěn and 纷 fēn.
享 (enjoy) — a picture of an ancestral hall where offerings were shared, hence to enjoy; it also appears in 亨 hēng and 郭 guō.

example.hanzi: 她喜欢在网上分享自己的旅行照片。
example.pinyin: Tā xǐhuan zài wǎng shàng fēnxiǎng zìjǐ de lǚxíng zhàopiàn.
example.english: She likes sharing her travel photos online.
example.fact: 分享 is reserved for sharing something enjoyable, useful, or emotionally positive (分享快乐 "share happiness," 分享经验 "share experience") — the dictionary gloss itself flags this with "esp. sth enjoyable," distinguishing it from plain 分 or 共享 for splitting up a cost or object more neutrally.

examples.hanzi: 我想和大家分享一个好消息。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng hé dàjiā fēnxiǎng yí ge hǎo xiāoxi.
examples.english: I'd like to share some good news with everyone.

examples.hanzi: 朋友们常常分享好看的电影。
examples.pinyin: Péngyoumen chángcháng fēnxiǎng hǎokàn de diànyǐng.
examples.english: Friends often share good movies with each other.

components.note: 衤 (clothing) — 衤 is the clothing radical, as in 衣, 裤, 衬; 被 is a quilt, then the passive marker.
皮 (pí) — loose hint — 被 is bèi; 皮 also sounds out 披 pī and 坡 pō.
扌 (hand radical, 提手旁) — actions by hand: 打, 拉, 抱; 捕 is to seize.
甫 (fǔ) is a loose clue; also in 铺 pù, 辅 fǔ, 薄 báo.

example.hanzi: 那名嫌疑人已经被捕。
example.pinyin: Nà míng xiányírén yǐjīng bèibǔ.
example.english: The suspect has already been arrested.
example.fact: 被 fronts the passive voice in Chinese (被捕, 被骗 "to be tricked," 被打 "to be hit") — historically 被 marked only misfortune or something done to someone against their will, which is why Chinese passive constructions still carry a faint negative flavor that English's neutral passive voice lacks.

examples.hanzi: 小偷昨天晚上被捕了。
examples.pinyin: Xiǎotōu zuótiān wǎnshang bèibǔ le.
examples.english: The thief was arrested last night.

examples.hanzi: 他因为开车喝酒而被捕。
examples.pinyin: Tā yīnwèi kāichē hē jiǔ ér bèibǔ.
examples.english: He was arrested for drinking and driving.

components.note: 土 (earth) — earth radical — a base is something solid on the ground, as in 地, 城, 块.
其 (qí) — loose hint — 基 is jī; 其 also sounds out 期 qī and 旗 qí.

example.hanzi: 这是学习汉语的基础。
example.pinyin: Zhè shì xuéxí Hànyǔ de jīchǔ.
example.english: This is the foundation of learning Chinese.
example.fact: 基 is a bound form meaning base: 基础 (foundation), 基本 (basic), 基地 (base), 基因 (gene). Several of the words use it together with 本 or 础, which also mean root or foundation.

examples.hanzi: 这个游戏的基本规则很简单。
examples.pinyin: Zhège yóuxì de jīběn guīzé hěn jiǎndān.
examples.english: The basic rules of this game are simple.

examples.hanzi: 这家公司的基础很好。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā gōngsī de jīchǔ hěn hǎo.
examples.english: This company has a solid foundation.

components.note: 后 (after, behind) — two words merged in simplified writing: old 后 "ruler" (皇后 empress) and 後 "behind, later" (as in 然后).
忄 (heart) — 忄 is the heart radical for feelings, as in 情, 怕; 悔 is regret.
每 (měi) — loose hint — 悔 is huǐ; 每 also sounds out 梅 méi and 海 hǎi.

example.hanzi: 我很后悔当时没有多陪陪家人。
example.pinyin: Wǒ hěn hòuhuǐ dāngshí méiyǒu duō péi péi jiārén.
example.english: I really regret not spending more time with my family back then.
example.fact: 后 ("after, behind") plus 悔 ("remorse," built from 忄 "heart") combine literally into "regret felt afterward" — framing regret in Chinese explicitly as something realized only in hindsight, once it is too late to change the outcome.

examples.hanzi: 如果现在不努力,以后会后悔的。
examples.pinyin: Rúguǒ xiànzài bù nǔlì, yǐhòu huì hòuhuǐ de.
examples.english: If you don't work hard now, you'll regret it later.

examples.hanzi: 我一点儿也不后悔做了这个决定。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ yìdiǎnr yě bú hòuhuǐ zuò le zhège juédìng.
examples.english: I don't regret making this decision at all.

components.note: 亻 (person) — a person and his word: 言 (speech) beside it gives a person who keeps his word, hence "trust, believe".
言 (speech) — written 讠 on the left of other characters, as in 说, 请, 谢.
亻 (person) — person radical — 仰 is a person looking up, as in 信仰 belief.
卬 (áng) — near sound — 仰 is yǎng; 卬 also sounds out 迎 yíng.

example.hanzi: 每个人都有权利选择自己的信仰。
example.pinyin: Měi gè rén dōu yǒu quánlì xuǎnzé zìjǐ de xìnyǎng.
example.english: Everyone has the right to choose their own beliefs.
example.fact: 信仰 is reserved for deep, often religious or ideological conviction (宗教信仰 "religious faith") — for an everyday "belief" or opinion about a fact, Chinese instead reaches for 相信 or 认为, keeping 信仰 for convictions that shape someone's whole worldview.

examples.hanzi: 我们应该尊重别人的宗教信仰。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen yīnggāi zūnzhòng biérén de zōngjiào xìnyǎng.
examples.english: We should respect other people's religious beliefs.

examples.hanzi: 她信仰佛教,每个月都去寺庙。
examples.pinyin: Tā xìnyǎng Fójiào, měi ge yuè dōu qù sìmiào.
examples.english: She believes in Buddhism and goes to the temple every month.

components.note: 亻 (person) — people, as in 你, 他, 们: 保 oldest form shows a person carrying a child on the back, so to protect.
呆 here is the old child shape 子 beside the person, a picture of keeping safe.
宀 (roof) — houses and shelter, as in 家, 字, 室.
女 (woman) — a woman at home under the roof: calm and safe.

example.hanzi: 大楼门口站着两名保安。
example.pinyin: Dàlóu ménkǒu zhànzhe liǎng míng bǎo'ān.
example.english: Two security guards stand at the building's entrance.
example.fact: 保安 began as a verb phrase meaning "to protect and ensure safety" (保 "protect" + 安 "safety") — over time it also came to name the person whose job is exactly that, a purely descriptive phrase calcifying into a job title.

examples.hanzi: 小区的保安每晚都会巡逻。
examples.pinyin: Xiǎoqū de bǎo'ān měi wǎn dōu huì xúnluó.
examples.english: The community's security guard patrols every night.

examples.hanzi: 进大楼前,保安要先检查你的证件。
examples.pinyin: Jìn dàlóu qián, bǎo'ān yào xiān jiǎnchá nǐ de zhèngjiàn.
examples.english: Before entering the building, the guard will check your ID.

components.note: 又 (hand) — the bottom, standing in for the 攴 (tap) of traditional 變. 亦 on top replaces the tangled-thread part and has no meaning link.
變 (traditional) — tangled threads and a tapping hand 攴: sorting out a mess, so 'change'. Read as 'usually explained'.
心 (heart) — feelings and attitudes: 想, 思, 感; 态 is one's attitude.
太 (tài) sounds exactly like 态.

example.hanzi: 蝴蝶是从毛毛虫变态而来的。
example.pinyin: Húdié shì cóng máomaochóng biàntài lái de.
example.english: Butterflies come from caterpillars through metamorphosis.
example.fact: 变态's original, neutral meaning is the biology term "metamorphosis" (变 "to change" + 态 "state, form") — its now-dominant colloquial sense, "perverted, abnormal," developed later as a figurative extension of "changed from the normal state," and the innocent biology usage still survives intact in scientific and textbook contexts.

examples.hanzi: 青蛙的变态过程非常有趣。
examples.pinyin: Qīngwā de biàntài guòchéng fēicháng yǒuqù.
examples.english: The metamorphosis of a frog is very interesting.

examples.hanzi: 这道题难得变态,全班只有一个人做对了。
examples.pinyin: Zhè dào tí nán de biàntài, quán bān zhǐ yǒu yí ge rén zuò duì le.
examples.english: This question is ridiculously hard, and only one person in the class got it right.

components.note: 女 (woman) — 女 marks women, as in 妈, 姐; 媒 is a matchmaker, as in 媒体 media.
某 (mǒu) — near sound — 媒 is méi; 某 also sounds out 煤 méi and 谋 móu.
亻 (person) — people, as in 你, 他, 做: 体 is a person's body.
本 (root) — the root of a person, the body; the traditional form was 體 with 骨 (bone).

example.hanzi: 这件事引起了媒体的广泛关注。
example.pinyin: Zhè jiàn shì yǐnqǐ le méitǐ de guǎngfàn guānzhù.
example.english: This matter attracted widespread media attention.
example.fact: 媒 alone already means "a go-between, a matchmaker" (as in 媒人) — 媒体 extends that old sense of an intermediary connecting two parties to modern mass communication, recasting newspapers, TV, and the internet as the go-between that connects information to the public.

examples.hanzi: 这个消息已经在媒体上传开了。
examples.pinyin: Zhège xiāoxi yǐjīng zài méitǐ shang chuán kāi le.
examples.english: This news has already spread in the media.

examples.hanzi: 现在很多年轻人通过社交媒体交朋友。
examples.pinyin: Xiànzài hěn duō niánqīngrén tōngguò shèjiāo méitǐ jiāo péngyou.
examples.english: Many young people now make friends through social media.

components.note: 走 (walk, run) — marks movement on foot, as in 起 rise, 越 cross, 超 surpass; 赶 is chasing or hurrying to catch up.
干 (gān) — gives the sound — 赶 is gǎn, same syllable with a different tone; 秆 gǎn and 肝 gān share it.
纟 (silk thread, simplified 糸) — threads, as in 红, 经, 系: a pulled-tight cord. The top part is also in 坚 jiān (firm).

example.hanzi: 快下雨了,我们赶紧回家吧。
example.pinyin: Kuài xiàyǔ le, wǒmen gǎnjǐn huí jiā ba.
example.english: It's about to rain, let's hurry home.
example.fact: 赶紧 always sits right before the verb it urges into action (赶紧走 "hurry and go," 赶紧吃 "hurry and eat") and cannot stand alone as a full predicate the way English "hurry!" can — its close cousin 赶快 is nearly interchangeable, differing mostly in a slightly more clipped, urgent register.

examples.hanzi: 时间不早了,你赶紧睡吧。
examples.pinyin: Shíjiān bù zǎo le, nǐ gǎnjǐn shuì ba.
examples.english: It's getting late, so hurry up and go to sleep.

examples.hanzi: 他赶紧把手机关掉了。
examples.pinyin: Tā gǎnjǐn bǎ shǒujī guān diào le.
examples.english: He quickly turned off his phone.
